title: State of Washington v. Eckenrode
facts: Petitioner Don Eckenrode was convicted of the manufacture and possession of marijuana while armed with a firearm in the Superior Court for Pierce County and sentenced. Eckenrode appealed the sentencing enhancement arising from the jury’s finding that he committed the crimes while armed with a firearm, asserting that the trial court erred in failing to instruct the jury that it needed to find a nexus between him, the manufacture and possession of marijuana, and the firearm. The Washington Court of Appeals affirmed Eckenrode’s sentence. Eckenrode appealed this decision to the Supreme Court of Washington.
questions: Did the trial court err in failing to instruct the jury that it needed to find a nexus between Eckenrode, the manufacture and possession of marijuana, and the firearm?
conclusions: Justice Chambers’ opinion for the Court affirmed the Washington Court of Appeals, concluding that although a nexus instruction is required in order to avoid subjecting defendants to sentencing enhancements for the mere exercise of their constitutional right to keep and bear arms, Eckenrode failed to request such an instruction at trial. Thus, as there was sufficient evidence to find that such a nexus existed, the Court held that there is no basis for reversing Eckenrode’s sentence.
